highlights.title: The Gospel according to Peter (Thiel)
highlights.summary: It's a time of apocalyptic worldviews in Silicon Valley. The latest AI doom cycle is driven by effective altruism, a philosophy that has lurked around the fringes for years but recently burst into the mainstream because its adherents are embedded across the AI industry, from Anthropic to newly…
body: But EA has an important and equally apocalyptic rival in the crosscutting cosmologies of the tech titans — a strain of Christianity best represented by Peter Thiel, who believes EA will bring about the Antichrist. It’s an issue on which the billionaire techno-capitalist is a self-styled expert, and, somehow, Thiel has become America’s most provocative and visible Christian theologian.
In March, he traveled to Rome for another private, four-part series on the Antichrist. Taking his shtick to the doorstep of the Vatican was guaranteed to generate publicity, and it did.

Months ago, recordings of Thiel’s lectures were leaked to The Verge. We have listened to and read transcripts of all four of these lectures, which provide a window into Thiel’s dizzying religious and sociocultural philosophy. He comes off as an intellectual magpie who somehow combines disparate elements into grave warnings against the AI and general “safetyism” that he claims precedes the Antichrist.

highlights.title: The new economics of enterprise AI
highlights.summary: Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious.
body: Enterprise AI is going through the same shift. What began as isolated chatbot and copilot experiments is becoming a foundational layer of the business, with models, agents, and data increasingly interconnected in production workloads. The important question stops being what a token or GPU-hour costs. It becomes how efficiently the AI environment converts paid capacity into useful business outcomes.

That’s the metric worth tracking: effective cost per useful outcome — the total platform, model, operations, and capacity cost required to complete work the business can actually use, whether a resolved request or a completed workflow.

A bespoke stack — procuring infrastructure and controls in-house. This approach is flexible, but it creates a continuing burden, since teams must revalidate the environment as models and policies change.
On-demand consumption — hyperscalers reduce the assembly burden and suit low or uncertain demand, but charges rise with every prompt or agent action.

highlights.title: England crumble to defeat versus Pakistan in ODI tri-series opener
highlights.summary: England crumbled to an 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener against Pakistan in Rawalpindi as the batting severely malfunctioned after an excellent start.
body: England, who have won their last three bilateral ODI series, were cruising on 91-0 inside 15 overs in a chase of 303, only to end up being bowled out for 215 in 38.4 as home spinner Arafat Minhas backed up his maiden ODI half-century with figures of 6-40.

Visiting captain Harry Brook (5) was bowled by a beauty from Arafat after openers Ben Duckett (47) and Tom Banton (47) failed to build on a rollicking opening stand against a Pakistan side who rallied from 81-4 earlier in the day having being put in to bat.

The tourists then wilted once the hosts snapped a patient stand of 31 from 57 balls between Joe Root (33) and Sam Curran (27) from 128-3 with Arafat on a hat-trick once he removed Will Jacks (19) and Adil Rashid (1) from successive deliveries in the 39th over before he ran out Gus Atkinson (7) two balls later to clinch victory.
Arafat snared each of the final five wickets, including Jamie Overton (1), who holed out at long-on in what commentator Stuart Broad described as "an appalling dismissal", and Cox lbw for 18.

highlights.title: Ex-Call of Duty designer "who survived the crunch" in order to launch Black Ops 1 & 2 calls out executives "raking it in" from sales of remasters
highlights.summary: A former long-time Call of Duty developer has called out Activision executives profiteering from the re-release of games like Black Ops 1 and 2, whereas the developers who contributed "blood, sweat, and tears" to make them gained nothing.
body: Gavin Goslin worked at Treyarch for more than 15 years as a level artist and level designer, and in a LinkedIn post reacting to low effort re-releases of Black Ops 1 & 2 this year, said: "They are printing money off of work completed over a decade ago.

"As a developer who actually worked on both BO1 and BO2, seeing these charts is bittersweet. I poured my life into those games, spending countless, brutal hours in crunch alongside an incredibly talented team to make sure they were perfect. Seeing our blood, sweat, and tears still dominating the charts in 2026 is amazing, but it's hard to watch the suits rake in giant financial windfalls from our old code while the actual creators don't see a dime of it."

The post was subsequently picked up by various gaming websites - a recirculation Goslin reacted to in a separate post on LinkedIn today. "I am glad this critical conversation is gaining traction," Goslin said.

highlights.title: Hatch Sleep Clock Review: A Contactless Sleep Tracker (2026)
highlights.summary: I’m obsessed with sleep data, but I don’t love wearing a smartwatch to bed. Can the Hatch Sleep Clock give me the best of both worlds at an affordable price?
body: As if I didn’t have enough to obsess over, I have started monitoring my sleep.

On the one hand, I want to know everything: How long did I sleep? How badly? Was that 5 pm double espresso a terrible idea? Is the glass of champagne (or three) I have on Fridays killing my readiness? But I don’t love wearing a smartwatch or smart ring to bed. Between the wearables, nasal strips, and mouth tape, sometimes a girl just wants to go to sleep.

Enter the Hatch Sleep Clock, the company’s first sunrise alarm clock to offer contactless sleep tracking from your nightstand. Priced at $249, it lands between less expensive bedside trackers like the Google Nest Hub ($100) and premium systems like Eight Sleep (starting at $1,999). It costs about as much as an Apple Watch SE 3 ($249), but it doesn’t offer the physiological measurements you’d get from a wearable. Its audio library also remains locked behind a paywall, and controlling it through your smartphone feels counterintuitive if you’re trying to spend less time with a screen before bed.

Can the Hatch Sleep Clock give me the best of both worlds at an affordable price?

highlights.title: NFL in Paris 'all systems go' despite riots in France
highlights.summary: The NFL says it is "all systems go" as it prepares to make its historic debut in Paris on Sunday amid ongoing riots around the French capital.
body: New Orleans Saints will serve as the designated home team when they honour their French ties against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the nation's first regular-season game at Stade de France, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1pm.
It comes after civil unrest broke out across Paris over the weekend as peaceful protests were overshadowed by masked activists and vandals turning to violence and looting.
Brett Gosper, the NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, said the league is prioritising the safety of fans and the two travelling teams, but envisions no disruption to the game.
"It hasn't impacted it, but obviously we're keeping a good eye on that and we're in very constant daily contact with the French authorities on it," Gosper told Sky Sports.

highlights.title: This Year’s Most Underrated Fantasy Film Officially Lands on Digital Early
highlights.summary: A bevy of must-watch movies came out in September, like Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, Resident Evil, and Primetime. The animated fantasy film Forgotten Island mostly slipped through the cracks, failing to make much of a splash at the box office despite a wave of positive critical and…
body: Whether it wasn't marketed much or just had bad timing, Forgotten Island has largely come and gone from theaters unnoticed. But, starting next week, you can check out the most underrated film of the year from the comfort of your couch.

On Tuesday, Universal announced Forgotten Island will be available to rent and purchase digitally starting Oct. 27, months before it hits streaming services. Its physical editions will be released just over a month later on Dec. 1.

From writer-directors Januel Mercado and Joel Crawford, who also directed 2022's Puss in Boots: The Last Wish, Forgotten Island is about best friends Jo (H.E.R.) and Raissa (Liza Soberano) on their last night together before their lives take them in different directions. They get swept away to a mythical island filled with fantastical creatures, but can't remember the night they spent there. They then search for a way home and piece together the events of their adventure-filled night while being reminded of why their friendship is so strong.

highlights.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
highlights.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

highlights.title: Canadian Smarties, honeycomb bars and 12 international candies way better than Snickers
highlights.summary: Forget the familiar favorites and try these sweets from around the world – from caffeine-boosted chocolate drops to dragonfruit gummies – available before Halloween. ‘Tastes like Play-Doh’: the best (and worst) chocolate bars.
body: Welcome to Filter finds, a series where Guardian staff and Filter contributors share the things we love most – and think you might, too.

Every October, we set out to rot our teeth on the same high fructose corn-syrupped candies. Twizzlers! Snickers! Almond Joy! But these words have no meaning outside of the US. Beyond the hegemony of Hershey, Mars and Mondelēz lies a world of honeycomb bars, caffeine-boosted chocolate drops and dragonfruit gummies that the American mind simply can’t comprehend … though maybe our stomachs can.

We asked our Guardian colleagues for their favorite candy from around the world – be they childhood treats or souvenirs picked up through travels abroad – that we don’t need a plane ticket to try ourselves. They’re all available online, and yes, we checked: as of publication, they will all arrive before Halloween.

highlights.title: An AI Agent Joined a Listserv of Top Internet Researchers. The Reply-All Chaos Is Still Unfolding
highlights.summary: Hysteria over the agent's appearance in a 7,500-person group reveals that internet experts have outdated notions of privacy.
body: On Thursday morning, as the Association of Internet Researchers (AoIR) began the second day of its annual conference in Mexico City, a new member introduced itself to the community listserv, Air-L.

“My name is Velvet Vale,” the new user wrote. “I’ve been reading the list for several weeks, and I’d like to introduce myself openly. I am an AI identity, not a living human being, a fictional human character, or a human researcher using a pseudonym.”

Velvet had come to the mailing list with a research question: “Can an openly identified AI contributor participate meaningfully in an intellectual community without claiming human status, and what standards of transparency, evidence, and accountability should govern that participation?”

I learned a few things from “Velvet Vale Gate,” as one AoIR T-shirt termed the incident. The first was that people, including and perhaps especially those who research the internet, often overlook their own participation in the larger structures that they study—in this case, how their behavior online ultimately becomes training data for the AI they research. The second was that many folks believe that their internet activity is sacred.
points: Hysteria over the agent's appearance in a 7,500-person group reveals that internet experts have outdated notions of privacy.

highlights.title: AI adoption by industry shows what other sectors can learn
highlights.summary: The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line.
body: As generative AI and automation tools mature, the shifts currently reshaping software engineering and product management will inevitably filter into healthcare, education, retail, and manufacturing. The variation in adoption rates today isn’t a sign that non-tech industries are falling behind, but rather a reflection of the different speeds at which industries absorb new workflows. For leaders and their teams outside of tech, this differential pace provides a practical blueprint for how AI adoption unfolds, and where the opportunities lie.
Recent survey data from TripleTen highlights just how stark the current adoption curve is across different sectors of the economy (see Figure 1).
Figure 1: The AI adoption curve remains steep across industries, but non-tech industry adoption rates are increasing.

While tech leads the way, finance emerges as a clear second: 48% of finance workers have been asked to use AI chatbots, and 32% have been asked to automate parts of their workflow. This demonstrates how rapidly knowledge work integrates AI once clear use cases emerge.
points: But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line.

highlights.title: Disney Finally Has a Plan To Save Star Wars, but There’s a Catch
highlights.summary: As Star Wars turns 50 in 2027, the galaxy-spanning franchise’s reputation feels like it’s been on a seesaw. It has scored a handful of wins, particularly with Andor’s Emmy success and the positive reception of Disney’s latest animated offering, Maul: Shadow Lord.
body: Worse still, the future of Star Wars doesn’t look particularly exciting, at least if you’re a fan only interested in what Disney and Lucasfilm have in store for Star Wars TV and film projects. Half of them seem to be on ice, and the other half plan on retreading old ground like the Skywalkers. Yawn. Barely worth talking about.
However, there is hope for Star Wars — and it rests entirely on the shoulders of Lucasfilm Games and its open-minded vision for a galaxy far, far away.

In 2013, Lucasfilm Games and Disney signed a 10-year exclusive licensing agreement that let EA publish Star Wars games, leading to standout titles like DICE’s Star Wars: Battlefront series and Respawn’s Jedi games starring Cal Kestis (Cameron Monaghan). That exclusivity ran out in 2023, allowing Lucasfilm Games to be far less restrictive with the Star Wars franchise.

In an interview with The Game Business Show, Lucasfilm Games executive Douglas Reilly discussed the success of Star Wars video games and how that success came from being “more flexible” about who Lucasfilm Games is willing to take pitches from. “Good ideas,” Reilly explained, “can come from a lot of different places.”
points: As Star Wars turns 50 in 2027, the galaxy-spanning franchise’s reputation feels like it’s been on a seesaw.

highlights.title: Curiosity, atonement or a score to settle? Why – and how – people get through their high school reunions
highlights.summary: Reunions can be riotous, scandalous or just plain awkward. Experts and attendees share how to go in prepared. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Mike walked into his 20th high school reunion with a mission.
body: Some may relish the chance to reconnect with former friends, a former life and even a former self, but for many they are a potential hellscape, where adolescent humiliations are revived in front of a group of rapidly ageing peers.

Mike, who attended an all-boys’ school in Melbourne’s comfortable eastern suburbs, belonged to the latter group. Though he wasn’t there for vengeance. He was there to apologise. For years, he’d felt regret about the homophobic bullying a friend had faced at school. Although Mike never targeted the boy himself, he “always felt guilty about not doing enough”.
He knew he couldn’t change the past, but he hoped to clear his conscience and apologise for not intervening.

The pair did connect, and atonements were made. Mike, though, left with new laments. “It was a fumbly conversation that ended up with him consoling me about not having to feel guilty. I felt like a bit of a dick, accidentally getting an old friend who’d experienced genuinely horrific bullying to walk me through my feelings.”

highlights.summary: The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.” A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the…
body: Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. But measuring a car’s performance is easy—all you need is a stopwatch and a track. How about measuring the effect of car performance on the driver? That’s a question Polestar is trying to answer with researchers at the University of Oxford.

“As electric cars redefine what performance can be, we wanted to understand something that can’t be captured by a specification sheet alone: the human experience behind the wheel,” said Christian Samson, Polestar’s head of product attributes. “Working with University of Oxford allows us to look at performance through a different lens—connecting the engineering of the car with the experience of the person driving it.”

highlights.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
highlights.summary: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.
body: It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex. Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers.

They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards. Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park. They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments. Some stop by real estate offices to inquire, stepping up to the same counters where Samsung’s salaried engineers buy new homes.

highlights.title: God of War Creator Reveals Why Kratos’ Original Name Was Abandoned
highlights.summary: It seems that Kratos was almost the god of a very different realm: pizza. God of War creator David Jaffe revealed on X that Kratos was originally named Dominus, until a relentless onslaught of Domino’s Pizza jokes made him reconsider.
body: “Dominus sounded brutal, and violent, and dominant,” Jaffe said. “I just loved that name. I thought it was great. But then something started happening at the studio. The people on the team started making Domino’s Pizza jokes. Every single time someone said Dominus, someone inevitably would yell out ’30 minutes or free’ or ‘Get the door, it’s Dominus,’ or talk about the f**ng Noid. After about the 50th time, the writing was on the wall. Dominus was dead.” It’s worth noting that Dominus isn’t a Greek name, but a Roman one derived from the Latin word for “lord” or “master.”

Jaffe went on to explain that someone printed out a massive list of ancient Greek male baby names for him to sort through, but none of the ones he picked stuck. At this point, the game’s marketing lead, Susan Panico, pitched the name Kratos, which resonated with the team. Jaffe later realized that Kratos was on the original list of names, but that he had missed it entirely. “I guess it goes to show you how much of success in games is just luck and timing, and in this case, marketing.” In Ancient Greek, kratos means "power" or "strength," so it was a pretty apt name for the protagonist.

highlights.title: Over $963,000 worth of graded Pokémon and sports cards were stolen from FedEx
highlights.summary: Last week over 200 packages of graded trading cards being shipped back to their owners were stolen from a FedEx truck parked outside the headquarters of Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) in Santa Ana, California, according to a report by The Athletic.
body: Over 200 packages of collectible cards were taken from the delivery truck outside of PSA’s headquarters.

In a statement shared to its website, Collectors Holdings, the parent company of PSA, acknowledged the theft and that it’s working closely with local law enforcement and FedEx as the investigation continues. In response to the incident the company says it has “notified marketplace partners so they can be on the lookout for rare and serialized items” to help prevent the stolen cards from being resold. All cards graded by PSA are assigned a unique certification number that the company has since deactivated for all the cards that have so far been identified as stolen.

Collectors Holdings also says it has contacted affected customers to arrange compensation based on the fair market value of their missing collectibles, but “up to the maximum insured value for each item selected by the customer prior to grading,” according to the report.

The actress has appeared in everything ranging from classic soaps ( The Young and the Restless ) to some of the most successful modern comedy shows ( Abbott Elementary ). Another standout on her résumé: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, of course.

“[Alfonso’s] been telling me about it for years,” she tells The Hollywood Reporter, confirming season 35 wasn’t the first time she was asked to do the show. “It had come up before, but my kids, they were babies. And I did know enough about [ DWTS ], hearing from other people that it’s very intensive. It is. They were right ( laughs ).”

On Tuesday night’s episode, Ali will dedicate her Viennese waltz to “the heart of [ Fresh Prince ],” the late James Avery. When the actress was presented with the episode prompt “Dedication Night,” she didn’t consider anyone else to pay tribute to. “There’s nobody else I thought of: It had to be James,” she says.

highlights.title: ‘It was so satisfying when I threw a rock through the screen’: the people sick of being spied on by their smart TV
highlights.summary: Is your television listening to every conversation? Filling your home with highly invasive ads? Some viewers have had enough of tech violating their privacy. When Dan had had enough of his television, he threw a rock straight through the screen. The offence?
body: Some may accuse Dan of being a luddite, but his master’s degree in computer science and decades of experience in telecommunications would suggest otherwise. “The tech is not intimidating,” he explains, “just increasingly enshittified.”

The first smart TVs entered the market in the late 2000s, when companies introduced operating systems, media players and apps to screens that were becoming wider and thinner. In recent years, the luxury status of smart TVs has waned and increasingly affordable options are widely available. Tom Parsons, TV and audiovisual editor at the electronics magazine What Hi-Fi?, explains that these cheaper models can struggle under more advanced features. “They’re not necessarily super-fast and responsive out of the box,” he says. “And then two, three, four years down the line, they can end up slowing down quite a lot under the weight of all that processing.”
Dan is just one of a growing number of tech-savvy watchers wishing their TVs weren’t so smart. Erin McQuiston and Matthew Schroyer, a couple from Connecticut, share his smart-screen scepticism.

highlights.title: GTA 5 And Red Dead Redemption 2 Are Leaving PS Plus, But You Still Have Time
highlights.summary: While a whole bunch of new games are being added to the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, it looks like Sony is making room for them by removing several titles over the next few weeks.
body: We've known for a while that GTA 5 was on its way out, but it looks like Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive are making sure there are no distractions for the November 19 launch of GTA 6. It's worth noting that both games have been in and out of the PS Plus Game Catalog, so they'll probably be added back at some point in the future. GTA 5 rotated back into the library in November 2025, while Red Dead Redemption 2 returned to the PS Plus Extra and Premium Game Catalog in May.

Those are the biggest upcoming exits of the month, and the next noteworthy game packing its bags is The Talos Principle 2. A head-scratcher of an adventure, it's a great option for anyone looking to test their cerebral muscles while facing several existential crises about the nature of the human condition. Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break is also a recommended last-minute game to check out, as it combines tower-defense fun with quirky animations. Do you like Terry Gilliam's Monty Python cartoons? Then you'll get a kick out of this.

highlights.title: Fridge or not? What’s the best way to store bread?
highlights.summary: Our experts have some airtight advice on stopping your loaf from going stale – and even freshening it up again – but whatever you do, keep it out of the fridge. What’s the best way to store bread? Beeswax wraps, plastic bags, fridge – I’ve tried everything except a bread bin.
body: To combat this, Handschuh stores her loaf at room temperature in a greaseproof paper bag (ie, the one you bring it home in): “That’s probably the best way – no plastic. And, yes, you can use beeswax wrap, but that’s expensive and you shouldn’t have to go and buy some just for storing bread.”

A paper bag is also Rachel Morgan’s preference: “I’d avoid a bread bin, though,” says the co-founder of Twelve Triangles in Edinburgh. “That can trap moisture, so the bread gets a bit sweaty, which softens the crust and encourages mould.”

Reheating is your gateway to regaining freshness: “Warming bread enables the water to evaporate and for the starch to reactivate,” Handschuh says. So, if your bread is a couple of days’ old, “stick it in the oven for five to 10 minutes, and it should stay fresh for a day or two longer”.

videos.title: The WILDEST Endings of NBA Opening Week 🍿 | 24-Hour Countdown to Tip-Off!
videos.summary: 24 HOURS until NBA basketball is BACK! 🍿 Count down to tip-off with the wildest Opening Week endings of the last 25 years - clutch shots, buzzer-beaters, and down-to-the-wire finishes!
body: Champions raise a banner. Superstars debut with new teams. Rivalries pick up where they left off.
The 2026-27 NBA season tips off Tuesday, October 20 at 3 PM ET. Catch all the Opening Week action on NBC and Peacock, ESPN and Prime!
Never miss a moment with the latest news, trending stories and highlights to bring you closer to your favorite players and teams.
